title: Assemble a slotted partition
instruction: Build the partition: stand the long slat on the white mark and slide both short slats down across it so their slots interlock.
context: Partitions for crates, cartons and fixtures are assembled from boards with interlocking slots; a board on edge tips over easily, so one hand steadies it on its mark while the other slides the crossing board down onto it.
setup: On the station table, three light brown rigid foam-board slats (16 mm thick, 8 cm tall, 40 g each), each standing on edge in a low grey plastic rack (two 3 x 0.8 x 2 cm blocks, 1 mm clear of the slat's faces; the long slat's rack is 10 cm from the slat's centre toward the middle of the table, and each short slat's is 4 cm from the slat's centre toward the arms). A long slat (30 cm) stands 18 cm in front of the arm bases, along the line between them, centred 15 cm to the right of centre; it has two slots 24 mm wide cut 4 cm down from its top edge, 18 cm apart. Two short slats (20 cm), each with one slot 24 mm wide cut 4 cm up from its bottom edge at its middle, stand pointing away from the arms, centred 28 cm in front of the arm bases: one 20 cm to the left of centre, one 22 cm to the right. A thin line of white tape on the table (6 mm wide, 30 cm long, along the line between the arms, centred between them, 27 cm in front of the arm bases) marks where the long slat goes.
scoring: 1.0 if both of the long slat's slots hold a short slat with the slots interlocked: all three slats standing on edge on the table, each short slat's centre within 6 mm of its slot along the long slat and within 6 mm across it, top edges flush within 4 mm, the long slat's centre within 2 cm of the white line's centre and the slat turned no more than 5 degrees from the line, all still for 1 second. Otherwise 0.4 for each interlocked crossing (0.8 for a full partition off the line). Slats laid flat in a cross, or resting on top of each other without interlocking, score 0.
reset_notes: Pull the slats apart and stand each back in its rack.
fidelity: Each slat is one rigid body built from boxes, its slots real gaps; 16 mm slats in 24 mm slots leave 4 mm of play each way. Surface friction in the slots isn't modelled beyond the station's default contact material, and each slat has the same 40 g, where a real short slat is a little lighter. Nothing is deformable.
